transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Ortiz (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Ari Sharma (HelioChain - Head Cloud Partnerships), Leah Kim (HelioChain - VP Partnerships), Devon Park (HelioChain - CTO)

[00:00] Maya Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. I'm Maya on the Redwood partnerships team, and Ethan is our solutions engineer. Quick round-robin?
[00:08] Ari Sharma: Hi all, Ari here. I'll hand over to Leah and Devon after a quick intro, but excited to learn more about Redwood and how we might partner.
[00:14] Leah Kim: Hi, Leah. We're looking at partner programs for GPU hosting and also systems integrators to help customers adopt LLM-powered features.
[00:20] Devon Park: Devon here; I'll focus on the infra and security side of things. We're evaluating options like reseller vs co-managed deployments.
[00:27] Ethan Park: Great. I'll do a brief tech overview later, but Maya can cover the GTM/partner models first.
[00:33] Maya Ortiz: Cool. High level — Redwood is an inference platform that runs hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. For partners like HelioChain we typically see three models: reseller/marketplace (you resell hosted API), dedicated-resell (you offer reserved capacity in your portfolio), or systems integrator where you bundle our private offering with your managed services.
[00:51] Ari Sharma: That matches what we were thinking. A few quick qualifiers from our side: primary customers are mid-market SaaS and a couple of regulated enterprise accounts; they need SOC2 level controls, some want VPC-only, and data residency is a must for a subset.
[01:06] Ethan Park: Understood. Our Private option supports VPC and on-prem and we integrate with KMS and HSM for key management. We also have audit logs and RBAC in the console. There are slight differences in telemetry and support levels between hosted and private but we can map them out.
[01:22] Leah Kim: On commercials, we care about unit economics — we want to package predictable pricing for our customers. Do you do partner margin split or reseller discounts?
[01:30] Maya Ortiz: Yes, we have partner pricing tiers. For dedicated/reserved pools there's an enterprise contract; for reseller of hosted API we offer partner discounts tied to committed volumes. We'll share the partner deck.
[01:38] Devon Park: From a tech POV, our concerns: latency for real-time apps, cost per token at scale, and also how we handle failover if a region's capacity is constrained. Can Redwood do smart routing across variants?
[01:48] Ethan Park: Yes — routing policies can prefer latency or cost, and we have automated fallback to compatible model variants if capacity is constrained. Also we do prefix/KV caching to reduce token cost and preserve latency SLOs.
[01:59] Ari Sharma: Sounds promising. For our managed customers, many will prefer we run the inference in our cloud footprint — e.g., we have GPU pools in APAC and EMEA. How does Redwood work in a multi-region partner-managed deployment?
[02:10] Maya Ortiz: For partner-managed Dedicated or Private, you can pin clusters per region, and Redwood's control plane supports multi-region orchestration. For private deployments you maintain the control plane connectivity and we provide the config and the runtime artifacts. There is a VPC connector for secure control-plane traffic.
[02:24] Leah Kim: A couple of compliance questions — do you have SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001? And what's your logging / audit retention?
[02:31] Ethan Park: We are SOC 2 and have an ISO roadmap. Audit logs are configurable; enterprise customers can send longer retention to customer-managed S3 or SIEM via push. For private we can keep logs on-prem per customer policy.
[02:43] Devon Park: KMS integration details — do you support customer-managed keys and HSM? We need separation for certain customers.
[02:49] Maya Ortiz: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated. We also support hardware-backed keys (HSM) integrations for certain enterprise contracts. We'll mark that as an action item to share the security doc.
[02:58] Ari Sharma: On the integration side — we'd like to offer two paths: 1) HelioChain resells Redwood hosted API and we handle onboarding; 2) HelioChain offers a managed Dedicated cluster running on our GPU fleet that customers can buy as part of our managed AI offering; and 3) SI engagements where we do custom integration. Which of these are easiest to enable quickly?
[03:16] Ethan Park: Resell of hosted API is fastest — self-serve onboarding and API keys. Dedicated/reserved pools take longer due to capacity planning and contract. SI engagements vary, but we have partner playbooks and an engineering onboarding flow.
[03:26] Leah Kim: For reseller model, can we get white-labeling or co-branding?
[03:30] Maya Ortiz: We support co-branding on the partner portal and partner-managed billing, but full white-label is limited because our hosted API endpoints are under Redwood domains. For reseller we can build an integration that masks some details and gives a HelioChain-branded onboarding experience.
[03:44] Devon Park: Network connectivity question — if we host Dedicated clusters in our cloud, how do agents in customer's VPC talk to the Redwood runtime? Is there direct peering or do we route via a connector?
[03:53] Ethan Park: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private link connectors. For Private on-prem it's usually a connector or 2-way VPN and an optional control-plane proxy. We'll need network diagrams from your infra team.
[04:05] Ari Sharma: Timeline — our sales cycles with these customers are typically 8–12 weeks. For an initial pilot, we'd prefer a 4–6 week technical pilot with a single customer who needs low-latency chat in EMEA. Is that a common engagement?
[04:18] Ethan Park: Absolutely. We run pilot programs. Typical pilot steps: share perf benchmarks, test on a small reserved pool or hosted with routing rules, instrument with Redwood Console for cost/latency dashboards, then expand to Dedicated.
[04:30] Maya Ortiz: We'll propose a pilot scope: one EMEA customer, 2–4 GPU nodes, target 100 qps peak, SLO 200ms p95 for short responses. We'll also provide an evaluation checklist for quality/regression monitoring.
[04:45] Leah Kim: That target seems reasonable. On the cost side, how do we estimate token costs? Do you provide a batch/caching recommendation per workload?
[04:53] Ethan Park: Yes — Redwood Optimize recommends batching and quantization settings based on workload. We'll take sample prompts and run a cost/latency profile. We'll also show how prefix caching can dramatically reduce per-token cost for session-based chat.
[05:06] Ari Sharma: A question on model catalog — do you ship with curated open models, and can we bring a custom model?
[05:11] Ethan Park: We have a model catalog with curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. You can bring your own model artifacts for Private/Dedicated; hosted has a vetted list but we can onboard more models through a model onboarding process.
[05:22] Devon Park: Data residency — some customers require that data never leaves EMEA and logs are stored locally. Can Redwood meet that with a partner-managed Dedicated cluster?
[05:30] Maya Ortiz: Yes, partner-managed Dedicated in your EMEA region can ensure inference and logs stay in-region. For hosted customers with residency needs we offer region restrictions and options to send logs to customer-managed storage in-region.
[05:43] Ari Sharma: Great. For the technical deep-dive, who should attend from Redwood? We want infra/network + someone who can speak to performance and batching.
[05:51] Maya Ortiz: Ethan will lead the deep-dive for performance and infra. We'll bring an infra architect if needed. Suggested attendees: Ethan, Maya, and possibly a Runtime Engineer.
[05:59] Leah Kim: Legal — we need an MSA template and a partner agreement. Any standard clauses we should expect? IP, data handling, indemnities, etc.
[06:07] Maya Ortiz: We'll share the partner agreement template and MSA redlines. Standard clauses include data handling, security SLAs, and indemnity language. For private deployments there's additional licensing terms.
[06:17] Devon Park: Can we get a quick sketch of the benchmark you'll run? We'd like latency p95, throughput, token cost, and multi-tenant isolation notes.
[06:25] Ethan Park: We'll run: 1) p95 latency and p50 for nominal prompt sizes; 2) throughput bench to find sustained qps on 2/4 GPU nodes; 3) cost per 1k tokens with and without caching; 4) memory/KV cache sizing. We'll share a spreadsheet with results.
[06:40] Ari Sharma: Sounds good. A few potential friction points from our customers: they often ask for SSO with SAML, SCIM for user provisioning, and role-based access for the console. Do you support those?
[06:51] Ethan Park: Yes — SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are available for enterprise accounts and Private deployments. RBAC is in the console with role templates we can extend.
[07:02] Maya Ortiz: Quick pause — anyone have blockers we should address now?
[07:05] Leah Kim: One blocker: HelioChain's sales org wants a predictable reseller margin and a simple onboarding flow so the customer purchase experience is smooth.
[07:13] Maya Ortiz: We'll include that in the partner commercial slide. We can show a sample price sheet and a margin tier.
[07:20] Devon Park: Another: our infra team will need a runbook for network setup and a security checklist.
[07:25] Ethan Park: We'll prepare a network runbook and the security checklist as part of the deep-dive materials.
[07:33] Ari Sharma: Great. Anything about hardware specifics — we run a mix of A100 and H100 nodes; some customers ask for quantized models on lower-memory GPUs. Does Redwood support quantization and different kernel selections?
[07:45] Ethan Park: Yes — the runtime supports quantization-friendly execution paths and kernel selection based on model architecture and hardware. We recommend configs per instance type; some customers use lower-memory GPUs with 4-bit quantization. We'll include recommended instance types per workload.
[07:58] Leah Kim: For billing, does Redwood support partner invoicing and BYOC billing?
[08:04] Maya Ortiz: We support partner-managed billing and can invoice customers through HelioChain. For BYOC (bring your own cloud), it's part of the Dedicated/Private model — billing depends on the contract and whether you want Redwood to meter usage or for HelioChain to do internal accounting.
[08:18] Ari Sharma: Do you have any public performance numbers we can show to customers?
[08:22] Ethan Park: We have performance profiles for the most common open models; we'll share a sanitized set of benchmarks and the methodology.
[08:30] Devon Park: Security auditors will want evidence of encryption in transit and at rest. Are these enabled by default?
[08:36] Ethan Park: Encryption in transit is default; at-rest encryption depends on storage config — customer-managed KMS ensures encryption at rest under customer keys.
[08:44] Maya Ortiz: Going back to GTM, does HelioChain have a target ARR or number of customers to onboard in Q2?
[08:51] Ari Sharma: We're aiming to onboard 3 managed customers in Q2 as an initial cohort. If pilots go well, we'll expand to a broader sales motion in Q3.
[08:59] Leah Kim: Okay. For the pilot, what's the minimum commitment or capacity?
[09:03] Maya Ortiz: For a pilot we can be flexible — typically a short-term reserved pool or hosted with routing rules. If you want dedicated capacity we discuss minimums during contracting.
[09:13] Ari Sharma: Let's talk risks — what would you say are the main migration risks for our customers?
[09:18] Ethan Park: Model performance/regression risk and network latency are top. We mitigate with evals, test harnesses, and a canary rollout capability. Also data access patterns can affect caching effectiveness, so we profile that in pilot.
[09:32] Devon Park: For the canary, can you do A/B or percent rollout per customer?
[09:36] Ethan Park: Yes, canary and A/B rollouts are supported and can be configured per route or per customer.
[09:41] Ari Sharma: Any concerns about licensing open model weights? Some customers want to bring models with restricted licenses.
[09:48] Maya Ortiz: We have an onboarding process for model licensing checks; bringing custom models is possible but we need to run vetting for redistribution/hosting rights.
[09:57] Leah Kim: Good. We're about halfway through. Can we sketch an initial timeline?
[10:02] Maya Ortiz: Sure: Week 0 (this week): NDA/partner intro materials. Week 1: share partner deck + security docs. Week 2: technical deep-dive and network runbook. Week 3–4: pilot setup and short bench runs. Week 5–8: pilot evaluation and go/no-go.
[10:18] Ari Sharma: That's in line with our expectations. For week 2 deep-dive, we'll have DevOps and network folks join.
[10:25] Ethan Park: We'll include lab credentials and a sample workload.
[10:29] Devon Park: On telemetry, will HelioChain get access to per-customer metrics in Redwood Console?
[10:34] Maya Ortiz: Yes — partners can see per-customer metrics and usage breakdowns with role-based views. For hosted reseller we can grant a partner portal view.
[10:44] Leah Kim: A question on security contacts — who should we send legal/security questions to?
[10:48] Maya Ortiz: Send them to partnerships@redwood.ai and security@redwood.ai. We'll also put a named contact in the follow-up email.
[10:57] Ari Sharma: Perfect. Any blockers on our side we'd need to surface?
[11:01] Leah Kim: I think we need to validate our internal billing flows and confirm margins; we'll follow up with a POC request form.
[11:08] Maya Ortiz: Great. Quick demo ask — Ethan, do you want to show a short Console walkthrough now or save for the deep-dive?
[11:14] Ethan Park: I'd prefer to save the full Console walkthrough for the deep-dive, but I can do a 3-minute highlight of dashboards and rollouts now.
[11:20] Maya Ortiz: Go ahead.
[11:21] Ethan Park: [screen share noises] Okay, in the Console you get per-route token cost, p95 latency, trace hooks, and rollout controls. Here's a mock route with canary set to 10%. You can see token-level cost showing caching savings.
[11:36] Devon Park: That's useful. Can you export audit logs to our SIEM?
[11:40] Ethan Park: Yes — logs can be pushed to your SIEM via S3 sink or pushed through an ELK connector.
[11:46] Ari Sharma: Anything else before we recap?
[11:48] Leah Kim: One last question: do you have partner case studies we can show prospective customers?
[11:53] Maya Ortiz: We have a couple of anonymized case studies; we'll include one that's similar profile to your mid-market use case.
[11:58] Maya Ortiz: Recap and next steps: Maya to send partner deck, security doc, and sample benchmarks; Ethan to prepare perf matrix and lab credentials; Ari to share infra specs and confirm pilot customer; schedule deep-dive for week of 2026-01-26. Action items as noted.
[12:14] Ari Sharma: Thanks everyone, looking forward to the follow-ups.
[12:17] Leah Kim: Thanks, bye.
[12:18] Devon Park: Bye.
